topics.title: What is Mockzilla?
topics.summary: Mockzilla is an MIT-licensed open source mock server for OpenAPI specs. The cloud platform at mockzilla.org builds and deploys mock servers for teams, free for small teams and students.

topics.title: Terminology
topics.summary: What Mockzilla's terms mean and why we chose them: simulations, specs, services, replays, contexts, scenarios, resilient backends and more.

topics.title: Install the CLI
topics.summary: How to install the Mockzilla CLI with Homebrew or a prebuilt binary, and when you need it at all.

topics.title: Quickstart: your first simulation
topics.summary: Create a sample simulation in the browser, deploy it, and call your hosted mock API in a few minutes.

topics.title: Simulation types
topics.summary: Four ways to run the same mock engine: app simulations in the browser, GitHub-deployed with a URL per branch, portable on your own machine, and codegen with real logic in the handlers.

topics.title: App simulations
topics.summary: The browser-built kind of simulation: compose your own specs, catalog APIs and static endpoints into one deployment with one URL, and iterate by editing in the app and deploying in seconds.

topics.title: Simulations from GitHub
topics.summary: Deploy simulations straight from a repository: one workflow step, a URL per branch and pull request, no account needed for the first push, and every change reviewed like code.

topics.title: Portable simulations
topics.summary: Run the same mock engine on your own machine: one command over a spec, a folder or a package, with hot reload on every file change and nothing leaving your computer.

topics.title: Codegen simulations
topics.summary: Generate a typed Go server from your spec: every handler serves the generated mock until you take it over with real logic, and the spec never leaves your repository.

topics.title: Create a simulation
topics.summary: The ways to start a simulation, what name, domain and slug mean, and when it starts serving.

topics.title: Start from the catalog
topics.summary: Browse the catalog of commonly requested provider APIs, see what each spec ships, and start a simulation from one in a click.

topics.title: Upload and update an OpenAPI spec
topics.summary: Upload an OpenAPI 3 spec in YAML or JSON, stay inside the size limit, tame large specs, and replace a spec without losing settings.

topics.title: Share links
topics.summary: Share a simulation with a link anyone can run locally, hand over a packaged file, or invite collaborators. No deploy needed.

topics.title: Run a simulation locally
topics.summary: Run any simulation on your own machine from its share link or a .mockz file, with the CLI, Docker, or Docker Compose.

topics.title: Deploy and URLs
topics.summary: What a deploy does and where a simulation answers: the available domains, why first deploys take a minute and redeploys seconds, taking unused simulations offline, and the soft build limits.

topics.title: Endpoints and static responses
topics.summary: Endpoints in a Mockzilla simulation: how their URLs are built, and how to add static endpoints with fixed responses you can change and redeploy in seconds.

topics.title: Service settings
topics.summary: Per-service settings in a Mockzilla simulation: mount path, upstream proxying with mock fallback, response caching, request and response validation, and spec options.

topics.title: Access control
topics.summary: Control who can reach a Mockzilla simulation: an API key on the mock API, credentials or a full switch-off for the API explorer, an IP allowlist, and runtime environment variables.

topics.title: Record and browse replays
topics.summary: Record a response once and serve it back for every matching request: the X-Mockzilla-Replay header, match keys on body, query and path fields, auto-replay, and editing recordings in the app.

topics.title: Export and import replays
topics.summary: Pack a service's recordings and replay settings into one portable file, and import it into any simulation: conflicts, size limits, and sharing a canonical fixture set with your team.

topics.title: Request history
topics.summary: Every request a simulation answers is recorded: browse and filter the log, open full request and response details, mask sensitive headers, and set per-service retention.

topics.title: Usage and limits
topics.summary: Watch what your simulations serve and what your plan allows: request and data transfer usage, throughput throttling, simulation and ref caps, and topping up a busy month.

topics.title: Resilient backends overview
topics.summary: What a resilient backend is: your own copy of a provider's API, with the same paths and responses, the failures their sandbox will not give you, and no shared vendor account. Payments and identity are available today.

topics.title: Add providers
topics.summary: How to add payment or identity providers to your organization: what a brand covers, how an order works, the free trial per type, and what removing one does to your sandboxes.

topics.title: Create a sandbox
topics.summary: Create a resilient-backend sandbox: what you need first, the three fields, picking which providers it serves, deploying it, and the URL your integration calls.

topics.title: Payments sandbox overview
topics.summary: What a payments sandbox does: the whole payment lifecycle with state, 3D Secure your tests can complete, hosted and redirect methods, idempotency keys, and the PSP's own response shapes.

topics.title: Payment scenarios
topics.summary: Drive a payments sandbox by naming the payment: every decline reason, the 3D Secure triggers, what to use when there is no cardholder, and which trigger wins when several match.

topics.title: Identity sandbox overview
topics.summary: What an identity sandbox does: subjects, documents, cases and the checks inside them, KYC and KYB in one API, hosted captures your tests can finish, and the provider's own report shapes.

topics.title: Identity scenarios
topics.summary: Drive an identity sandbox by naming the subject: every refusal reason, the review, pending and hosted outcomes, what reaches a subject you did not name, and which trigger wins.

topics.title: Write your own scenarios
topics.summary: Add scenarios of your own to a sandbox: where they live, which layer wins, the editor and the YAML behind it, what is validated before a save, and how to scope one.

topics.title: Change values with contexts
topics.summary: Replace the values a sandbox returns: what a context is, when you need one, how names match at any depth, how scopes stack, and what the sandbox still checks at runtime.

topics.title: Sandbox activity
topics.summary: Browse what a sandbox has done: the lists each type keeps, what the columns show, searching by reference, filtering, one provider at a time, and how long records last.

topics.title: Pin a build version
topics.summary: Hold a sandbox on one build instead of following the latest: where the control is, when pinning helps, what a build change adds or drops, and how long a build stays deployable.

topics.title: CLI reference
topics.summary: Every command and flag of the Mockzilla CLI: serving a spec, folder or package, inspecting and simplifying a spec, packing a folder, and running a simulation from your account.

topics.title: GitHub Action
topics.summary: The portable and codegen actions: the workflow to copy, every input, what a run gives back, the URL each branch gets, and what each failure means.

topics.title: MCP server for AI agents
topics.summary: Let Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or Gemini CLI run mock APIs for you: what to add to your agent's config, the tools it gets with no account, and how to log in to deploy to your organization.

topics.title: Preferences and password
topics.summary: Language, date format, timezone and your password on the General tab of Settings, plus how to add a password to a Google or GitHub account and how to delete your account.

topics.title: Connected accounts
topics.summary: Connect Google or GitHub to your Mockzilla account, what a GitHub connection gives you beyond signing in, and what happens if you disconnect your last sign-in method.

topics.title: Members and invitations
topics.summary: Add people to your organization and manage the ones who are in it: change a role, remove someone, invite by email with a scope, resend or revoke a pending invitation, and how seats are counted.

topics.title: Roles and permissions
topics.summary: The four organization roles and what each one can do, task by task: simulations, sandboxes, members, API keys, single sign-on, the audit log and billing. Plus roles on one simulation and on an API key.

topics.title: Organization name and URL
topics.summary: Rename an organization and pick its URL slug: what the slug does to simulation addresses, the rules it has to follow, and when it stops being editable.

topics.title: Set up single sign-on
topics.summary: Put your organization behind your own identity provider: pick one of nine, fill in the OpenID connection, decide whether members must use it and for how long a sign-in lasts, and verify the email domains that route to it.

topics.title: Access defaults
topics.summary: Set an API key, explorer credentials and an IP allowlist once for every simulation in the organization, and see how a single simulation overrides one of them or hands it back.

topics.title: API keys
topics.summary: Issue keys for calling the Mockzilla API from scripts and CI: the two roles a key can have, how to send it, what revoking does, and how many keys an organization can hold.

topics.title: Audit log
topics.summary: Read what changed in your organization and who changed it: what each row holds, which actors appear, what is recorded and what is not, and how to narrow the list by period.

topics.title: Plans and limits
topics.summary: What your plan allows, where to read it in the app, how to switch plans or change the way you pay, and what happens to your simulations if you cancel.

topics.title: Request top-ups
topics.summary: Buy extra requests on top of your monthly allowance: one-time or recurring, how they are priced and how long they last, what drains first, and what a plan change does to them.

topics.title: Backend add-ons
topics.summary: How providers are billed: they join the subscription you already have, what a price change does to a brand you hold, and what removing one or losing your plan does to the charge.

topics.title: Invoices
topics.summary: Where to find what your organization was charged: what lands on one invoice, how to read the list, opening the full copy with its PDF, and why the list can be empty.

topics.title: Student plan
topics.summary: A free plan for students: what you need before applying, what the form asks for, how the review works, and how to give the plan back.

topics.title: Get support
topics.summary: Report a bug, ask for a feature or get help from the Support page in your workspace: how to open an issue, who can read it, and what its status means.

topics.title: Contact us
topics.summary: Reach Mockzilla without an account: the contact form, the addresses for education and privacy questions, and how to tell us about a docs page.

topics.summary: This page explains the request flow through Mockzilla and how different features interact.

topics.title: Portable Mode
topics.summary: Run a mock server directly from OpenAPI specs and/or static response files.

topics.title: Docker Compose
topics.summary: Run Mockzilla as a container alongside your app.

topics.title: Codegen Mode
topics.summary: Codegen mode generates typed Go code from your OpenAPI specs, giving you compiled services with custom middleware, typed request/response handlers, and a single binary you can deploy anywhere.

topics.title: Templates
topics.summary: GitHub templates to quickly start a new project with Mockzilla.

topics.title: Services
topics.summary: A service is one collection of API endpoints.

topics.title: Factory
topics.summary: The Factory provides programmatic generation of mock requests and responses from Go code, without running the HTTP server.

topics.title: App Configuration
topics.summary: App-level configuration for Mockzilla server.

topics.title: Service Configuration
topics.summary: Each service can have its own `config.yml` file that controls runtime behavior like latency simulation, error injection, validation, and caching.

topics.title: Code Generation Configuration
topics.summary: The `codegen.yml` file controls how Go types and handlers are generated from your OpenAPI specification.

topics.title: Replay
topics.summary: Record API responses and replay them on subsequent requests that match specific request fields.

topics.title: Storage
topics.summary: Mockzilla uses a layered storage architecture that provides service isolation while sharing a single backend connection.

topics.title: Custom Middleware
topics.summary: Compiled Go services support custom middleware for advanced use cases like authentication, logging, request modification, and stateful behavior.

topics.title: Contexts
topics.summary: Contexts provide a way to control the values generated for API responses and requests.

topics.title: Fake Functions
topics.summary: Every fake function a context can use to generate a value, such as fake:address.city.

topics.title: Service Command
topics.summary: The service command generates a complete service from an OpenAPI spec or static files.

topics.title: Simplify Command
topics.summary: The simplify command reduces the complexity of large OpenAPI specs by removing union types (anyOf/oneOf) and limiting the number of optional properties per schema.

topics.title: Lint Command
topics.summary: The lint command finds schemas in an OpenAPI spec that no value can satisfy.
